properties.work_desc: 400 m line of workings with 3 shaft areas. Deepest shaft 30m, also shallower diggings.

properties.all_names: Princess Alexandra, Princess Alexandra Extended, Princess
properties.hostrocks: andesite - Cunningham Formation;  siltstone - Cunningham Formation;  slate - Cunningham Formation
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: On the same line as Poormans. This occurrence consists of at least 2 shafts and an open cut. The gold mineralisation is contained in  quartz veins striking 295 dip 45E in slate and siltstone and was worked to depth of 27m.
properties.work_desc: At least 2 shafts deepest 27 m, Open pit(dimensions unknown) and shallow pits.

properties.hostrocks: siltstone - Cunningham Formation;  slate - Cunningham Formation
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Auriferous quartz vein (thickness unknown) striking 295, dip 45 E in slates and siltstones. Location uncertain, reportedly on the same line of workings as Princess Alexandra and Poormans.

properties.reference: () MR01475;  Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Workings consist of shafts and surface workings located on an auriferous quartz vein which strikes approx. 300 mag in siltstones. Dimensions of the vein are unknown.

properties.hostrocks: sandstone - Cunningham Formation;  siltstone - Cunningham Formation
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: The occurrence is a auriferous quartz vein with shafts sunk into the quartz. The mining lease strikes 295. Location not certain. Spears' Mine in GL64 is also reportedly in this area (MR01475).

properties.hostrocks: conglomerate - Cunningham Formation;  siltstone - Cunningham Formation
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: An auriferous quartz vein related to a minor fault or shear. The vein is up to 30cm thick and pinches into a leader.
properties.work_desc: Shafts and shallow pits, dimensions unknown.

properties.hostrocks: greywacke - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group;  slate - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: Shafts and pits extend over a over 400m zone containing a auriferous quartz lode (minor sulphides) on a fault striking 320, dipping steeply W. The gold is in a highly fractured narrow crush zone on hanging wall side. Vein generally < 25cm.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Cunningham Formation;  siltstone - Cunningham Formation;  slate - Cunningham Formation
properties.summary_desc: Location is approximate and few records exist. Presumambly an auriferous quartz vein in slates and siltstones. Worked from shafts and shallow pits.
properties.work_desc: Shafts, deepest more than 15m and trenches. One line of workings strikes approx. 290.

properties.hostrocks: sandstone - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Shafts and pits into an auriferous quartz lode containing significant iron staining. The vein is reportedly 20cm wide in slate. Leaching and oxidation present but to what extent is unknown.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Shafts and pits on an auriferous quartz vein. The vein strikes 350 deg mag and dips to the east. The vein system is hosted by slates. Depth of the workings is unknown.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: An 1.2m thick auriferous quartz vein with shafts (to 45m depth) and trenches. Workings appear to be at an intersection of E-W and N-S veins (Matson).
properties.work_desc: Shafts, deepest 45m, drives, stoping, adits, trenches.

properties.summary_desc: Shaft and pits suggest a 350 striking reef of up to 1.8m thick. The strike length is about 200m. Little known, maybe part of Great Britain Mine.
properties.work_desc: Shaft(s), depth unkown and surface diggings.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: An auriferous quartz vein of unknown dimensions that strike 350 and dips 75 E. Sulphides were probably present as historic records indicate that mercury was "sickened". Chump Mine and Hughes Reef are possibly on the same reef.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group;  tuff - Crudine Group
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: A 30-40cm thich auriferous quartz (sulphide?) vein hosted by siltstone, tuff and andesite.
properties.work_desc: At least 3 shafts, deepest deeper than 20m.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: An auriferous quartz vein for which dimensions and attitudes are unknown. The proximity of Monks Mine and Chump Mine suggest that all three on same reef if so;- strike is north-south and dips east, host rocks are siltstone and andesite.
properties.work_desc: Shaft  deeper than 18m and  presumambly associated drives.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Presumambly a auriferous quartz vein hosted by siltstone. Very little known. Supposedly near Monks Mine. AMG from Matson 1975.

properties.all_names: Kaiser Wilhelme, Prince Wilhelme, Prince Billy, Golden Gully, King Billy Mine, Billy
properties.summary_desc: This is the largest producer in the area with a strike length 600m. The mineralized zone is a 30m wide stockwork of  coarse 0.3-1m wide veinlets making up 10% of rock in faulted contact between crystal tuff and phyllite.
properties.work_desc: Number of shafts, deepest 228m in southern area Drives at15, 76, and 137m. Open cut near main shaft.

properties.hostrocks: phyllite - Cunningham Formation;  siltstone - Cunningham Formation
properties.summary_desc: A North west striking, steeply W dipping fault controlled narrow (0.2-1m) auriferous quartz lode flanked by a narrow puggy zone, Iron-stained phyllite. In open cut prolific quartz veins strike 325 / Vert and 285 / 72 S.
properties.work_desc: Shfts, deepest 55m, numerous surface workings. Open cut 25x40m, 10-15m deep in the southern part of workings.

properties.hostrocks: siltstone - Crudine Group;  slate - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: Workings have a 400m strike length with the mineralisation in being in  2m wide auriferous quartz veins and interbedded siltstone.
properties.work_desc: Shafts, deepest 24m. Shallow pits. Open cuts 20m x 5m and 40m x 30m x 4m deep.

properties.summary_desc: An 22cm wide auriferous quartz vein in siltstone which yielded 30.6 g/t prior to 1870's. The workngs consist of shafts, (deepest 46m) and shallow pits. The strike is north-south and may dip steeply east. Very little known.
properties.work_desc: Shafts, deepest 46m with 40m drive at the bottom,  pits.

properties.hostrocks: siltstone - Crudine Group;  slate - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: The Main lode is 30cm wide and consists of auriferous quartz vein material with pyrite and arsenopyrite. The vein strikes 330 dip 45 E in siltstones. Some alluvial workings present. The Saxon Shaft is in the northern part where the reef curves to 035.
properties.work_desc: Shafts, deepest 91m, shallow pits, alluvial workings in southern area.

properties.hostrocks: siltstone - Crudine Group;  slate - Crudine Group
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: This is an auriferous, 25-30cm wide, quartz vein with minor sulphides (arsenopyrite, pyrite). The records indicate that the workings extend to 108m depth and was heavily mineralised.  Leaching and economically important oxidation present.
properties.work_desc: Shafts, deepest 90m, 76m on underlay, shallow diggings.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Presumambly an auriferous quartz vein in siltstone. Strike probably N-S, extent and nature of the workings is unknown. East of Stringy Bark Mine.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Presumambly a narrow Auriferous quartz (sulphide) vein in sediments which has been worked to shallow depths. Few details known.
properties.work_desc: At least 2 shafts both deepr than 15m and shallow diggings.

properties.summary_desc: Ter workings at this site include a 50m costean 6m deep which follows a narrow auriferous quartz vein with minor sulphides and striking 020 in slates.

properties.hostrocks: siltstone - Crudine Group;  slate - Crudine Group;  tuff - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: The occurrence is an narrow auriferous quartz vein, which strikes east-west, dip unknown. The mine dumps contain banded quartz with visible sulphides. Ferruginous quartz outcrops in viscinity.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: This is an auriferous quartz (minor  sulphide) vein with a shaft to 73m. in siltstone.  The vein curves from strike 300, dip 80E to 225, dip 30S and is mineralised down to 73m. In 1912 a 10cm vein yielded 46.6g/t. Leaching and oxidation to 24m depth.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: The occurrence consists of several shafts located on a 23cm wide auriferous quartz vein which is mineralised to at least 16m. The vein strikes 300 and dips west at 60 deg  in siltstones. Oxidation and leaching present, but extent unknown.
properties.work_desc: Several shafts at least 17m deep, surface diggings.

properties.summary_desc: A tunnel of unknown dimesions driven into a 15cm thick auriferous quartz vein, which strikes 305 and dip 45SW. No other information.
properties.work_desc: Tunnel, dimensions unknown and surface diggings.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Workings consist of shafts of unknown dimensions. The nature of the mineralisation is unknown however it is presumed to be an auriferous quartz vein. The vein is reported as curving from N-S strike to W and dips E.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Cunningham Formation;  siltstone - Cunningham Formation
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Reportedly a quartz vein with a black seam possibly oxidised iron-minerals. Bell won $9000 worth of very fine Au from the vein at the turn of the century.
properties.work_desc: Shafts and open cut of unknown dimensions.

properties.hostrocks: crystal tuff - Crudine Group;  phyllite - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: A north east trending, steeply north west dipping,  auriferous pyritc quartz-calcite vein with chalcopyrite and galena, hosted by chloritic crystal tuff (minor alteration). The vein is near and at the contact with phyllite.
properties.work_desc: 4 horizontal adits at different leves into the hill side, longest 152m. Shafts and stoping between levels.

properties.hostrocks: rhyolite - Crudine Group;  shale - Crudine Group;  tuff - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: A north-south striking east dipping auriferous quartz-calcite vein stockwork with pyrite, arsenopyrite and chalcopyrite.  Stockworks make up 5-10 % of rock in rhyolite and tuff, both sheared and brecciated. Mineralisation terminates at contact with shale.
properties.work_desc: 110 m adit driven in to the side of the hill.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Very little known, the location and the reported grades are tho only records. This is presumably an auriferous quartz vein in siltstone and andesite. Could be related to Specimen Hill, Quartz Hill, Manna Hill group of mines.

properties.hostrocks: sandstone - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group;  tuff - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: Gold found in three settings; NW trending shears, EW trending shears & tuff/shale contact. Mineralisation appers to be related to a shear zone lode and minor lode intersections. No payable ore was found below 24m depth suggesting the effect of oxidation.
properties.work_desc: Zone 30x200m. 3 adits, longest 80m. Shafts 73m, 23m, 21m. Open cut 30x12m, 8m deep . shallow surface diggings.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: This is a auriferous quartz vein in siltstone and andesite. Dimensions and strike are unknown. Occurrence maybe related to Quartz Hill, Manna Hill, Specimen Hill group of mines.

properties.hostrocks: andesite - Crudine Group;  quartzite - Crudine Group;  siltstone - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: This is an auriferous quartz vein occurrence with pyrite, arsenopyrite, chalcopyrite and sphalerite. The workings extend over a large area and are located on a south plunging saddle reef. Mineralisation in ironstained quartzite, siltstone and andesites.
properties.work_desc: Adits driven northward into hill. Numerous shallow shafts, 6-15m deep over area of 100m x 200m.

properties.summary_desc: This is a Tertiary deep lead with  a 70m tunnel trending 270mag and a 6m cross drive at 50m. The Main tunnel opens to a 6x6x6m room at the end.
properties.work_desc: 70m tunnel due 270 with a 6m cross drive at 50m. Tunnel has a 6 x 6x 6m dug out at its end.

properties.summary_desc: Two shafts 17 and 35m and two adits, the longest is over 130m, developed on a auriferous quartz vein. The details of  the mineralisation and  production are unknown however the extensive workings suggest a significant mine.
properties.work_desc: 2 shafts 17m and 35m with drives. 2 adits 100m apart,  maximum length over 130m.

properties.summary_desc: This is a Tertiry  deep lead with 12 adits 40-80m long on the northern and eastern flanks of the hill. Permian sandstone and conglomerate occur beneath the basalt. Strike of lead may be 140(from Dubbo 1:250 000 sheet).
properties.work_desc: 12 adits, longest 80m generally 40-80m.  In 1937 one old tunnel 12m long, extended to 60m by 1938.

properties.all_names: Bald Hill Lead; Bald Hill,  Ivesons Tunnel
properties.summary_desc: At least 47 tunnels into a lead up to 12m wide beneath a Tertiary basalt. The gravels rest on conglomerates, shales, slates and sandstones.
properties.work_desc: At least 47 tunnels into the hill, longest  ones reported 140m, 152 m and 177m.

properties.hostrocks: clay - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  silt - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: Geochemical anomaly of 6.5ppm Au in Tertiary deep lead under a basalt cap in a point-bar sequence. Within the sequence there are several layers of potential Au-bearing material.
properties.work_desc: Grab sampling of gravel over 2.5km distance east from Bald Hill, only a few samples collected.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a) ;  Matson C.R. (1972) GS1972/220
properties.summary_desc: A Tertiary deep leads under a basalt cap. Two tunnels; 122m tunnel striking north-south and 213m tunnel striking approximately 290.
properties.work_desc: 2 tunnels: 122m tunnel striking N-S and 213m tunnel striking approximately 290.

properties.hostrocks: gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a) ;  Matson C.R. (1972) GS1972/220;  Wilkinson C.S. (1877)
properties.summary_desc: Dredging and sluicing operations at the junction of Muckerawa Creek and Macquarie River. The wash was 9-21m thick.

properties.hostrocks: gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: Alluvial gold workings along Muckerwa Creek over an area of approximately 500 x 100m.
properties.work_desc: Shallow alluvial diggings over an area of 500x100m.

properties.hostrocks: gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a) ;  Matson C.R. (1972) GS1972/220
properties.summary_desc: Worked for alluvial gold in 1883-1885 by Junction Point Company. Site presently under Lake Burrendong. Gold, sapphire, ruby-rich alluvial gravels recovered from deep leads, mostly dredged late last century. Minor garnet and topaz is also present.

A Tertiary deep lead with cemented wash under the basalt cap. The wash averages 0.6-3m in depth and is located 152m above the Macquarie River.  In 1894 at least 20 men worked on this deposit. In 1933 150 loads yielded 186g of Au .

properties.hostrocks: gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a) ;  Matson C.R. (1972) GS1972/220
properties.summary_desc: Alluvial workings, in 1883 2705 g obtained from first paddock. Pump employed for sluicing. Site currently under Lake Burrendong. Later the area was worked by C.L. Garland's Dredge (later called Macquarie Enterprise Syndicate) between 1899 to 1917.

properties.hostrocks: gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.production: :?m3 estimated production for  0.009019t Au   :553000m3 actual production for  0.27t Au   :?m3 estimated production for  0.00187t Au
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a) ;  Matson C.R. (1972) GS1972/220
properties.summary_desc: Area worked by a number of groups around 1901-1903, and 1936-19367. In addition the area was worked by C.L. Garland's Dredge as part of a much larger area.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a) ;  Matson C.R. (1972) GS1972/220
properties.summary_desc: An Tertiary deep lead under a basalt cap. A 47m long tunnel was driven into the slate and 25m of drives in gravel, in 1934, however the area was worked years prior to this. The deep lead is situated about 122m above the present river level.
properties.work_desc: 47m long tunnel in slate and 25m of drives in gravel.

properties.reference: MARSHALL C.W. (1963) GS1963/131;  Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: A Tertiary deep lead beneath a basalt cap. 6-9m rises from tunnel to wash which is from a few cm to 3.5m thick. About 183m above Macquarie River level. Confederate Tunnels approx. 750m south of these workings.
properties.work_desc: 2 tunnels, longest 183m.  6-9m rises from tunnel to wash.

properties.hostrocks: basalt - Ungrouped Cenozoic igneous units - volcanic;  gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.reference: MARSHALL C.W. (1963) GS1963/131;  Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: A Tertiary deep lead beneath a basalt cap. Four tunnels, the longest is 95m with 6-9m rises from tunnels to the wash. The wash ranges from a few cm to 3.5m thick and has a lateral extent of 50m x few hundred metres. Wash includes white quartz pebbles.
properties.work_desc: 4 Tunnels, longest 95m 6-9m rises from tunnels to wash.

properties.all_names: Horse Bald Hill, Burma Malay Company
properties.hostrocks: basalt - Ungrouped Cenozoic igneous units - volcanic;  gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: An auriferous Teriary deep lead under a basalt cap. A number of workings cover a 15 hectare area. The wash was up to 4m thick but average grades only 1g/m3. Whether this site is the same as Matsons (1975) no.215 is not absolutely certain.
properties.work_desc: Workings cover about 15 hectares and consists of adits and pits. At least 366m of tunnels.

properties.hostrocks: basalt - Ungrouped Cenozoic igneous units - volcanic;  gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: An auriferous Tertiary deep lead under a basalt cap. Rises from a number of tunnels to 4m thick wash. Gold grades patchy.  About 24.4m above present river level. The basalt cover is 61m thick. Regent Resources N.L. surveyed area in 1989.
properties.work_desc: Number of tunnels/adits at least 107m in total. Open cut, dimensions unknown. Shafts, rises and drives, depths unknown.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: A Tertiary deep lead under basalt cap. No records. According to Matson, adjacent to portion 77 parish Coolamin.
properties.work_desc: Presumambly tunnels and shafts, no data.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Tunnels driven into a Tertiary deep lead under basalt cap. No other information.

properties.hostrocks: basalt - Ungrouped Cenozoic igneous units - volcanic;  gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: The fossil placers (deep leads) are perched above the Macquarrie River and consist of auriferous gravels containing white quartz pebbles overlain by Tertiary basalts. A adit has been driven in siltstones under the deep lead.

properties.hostrocks: gravel - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: In 1977-78 the site was sampled by Geological Survey of NSW to determine the present gold content. The tailings cover an area about 125x25m with average 10cm thickness. They contain 200-400m3 of  material at ave. grade of 1ppm Au.

The material at this location contains about 1.4ppm Au. Quantity of material is not sufficient to make location economic. Batteries oprated in this area in 1877-1904. Tailings were treated in 1934 and 2737 g of Au was recovered from 3687 m3 of material.
properties.work_desc: Old battery site. Tailings treatment site.

properties.hostrocks: arenite - Cunningham Formation;  slate - Cunningham Formation
properties.summary_desc: Only records of workings on this location is the report of discovery in ARDM 1920 p105-106.  Whether the prospect was ever worked as a mine is unknown. Locality is not exact as it was reported only as being in Portion 65 Parish Cooper.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: The location is uncertain however the records indicate that an auriferous quartz vein (2.5-7.5cm wide) was worked in1935. The vein which pinches out at 9m in slates, grades poor.
properties.work_desc: Shafts and shallow pits dimensions unknown.

properties.hostrocks: sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  silt - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: A weak geochemical anomaly in the upper reaches of Middle Creek. The anomaly (602ppb Au) are thought to be due to small scale auriferous quartz vein outcrops in the area. Area was explored by BHP UTAH in 1988

properties.hostrocks: sand - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  silt - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units
properties.summary_desc: Stream sediment survey by BHPG in 1990 uncovered a weak Au anomaly 48.5ppb in Molwran Creek. Anomaly is probably related to Tertiary deep leads in the area.
Few details are known about this occurrence. The located of minig lease GL 356 is on Parish Map in MR3556. Worked by R . Kloot and Co. in 1890's. Lease runs north-south.
An auriferous quartz vein of unknown dimensions. The mining lease trend north-south. Few details known. Location of Mining Lease GL 130 from Parish Map in MR3556, workings from GS1981/185.
properties.work_desc: At least one pit and trench, dimensions unknown.

properties.summary_desc: An auriferous quartz vein with a series of workings includind an open cut. The vein trends north-south. Estimated original depth  of open cut is10-15m. Strike length about 500m.
properties.work_desc: Open cut originally 10-15m deep, partly fillled in.

properties.summary_desc: The occurrence consists of an auriferous quartz vein with shallow workings that trend north-south and north west. The reef is approximately 50m long. Original depth estimated to be 8-10m.
properties.work_desc: Shallow workings approximately 50m long, estimated original depth 8-10m.

properties.summary_desc: Location of GL 113 given on Parish Map in MR3556. Lease runs NNW. No other data available - presumambly worked for gold.
The occurrence is a quartz reef of unknown attitude and dimensions, located on GL 150 and worked by worked by Edwards in 1916. Lease runs NNW. Location of GL 150 from Parish Map in MR3556.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: These are 11.2m and 5m shafts located on an 2-3m wide auriferous quartz (minor sulphide) vein which strikes 285 and dips 70E. The vein is hosted by slates in a fault or a faulted contact. Reportedly similar to Kurrajong Reef.
properties.work_desc: 11.2m shaft inclined at 70 deg E with drives of 8.8m to the NW and 14.3m to the SE. A 5m shaft also nearby.

properties.summary_desc: A 13.7m shaft and shallow diggings located around an auriferous quartz vein. Mining lease runs NNW (may indicate the direction of the reef?) . No other information. Location on Parish Map in MR3556 - GL 351. Robert Thompson worked the area in 1890's,

properties.hostrocks: sandstone - Crudine Group;  slate - Crudine Group
properties.summary_desc: Reportedly two sub-parallel auriferous quartz reefs. The reefs were mined by shallow shafts and 3 or 4 short adits. The Eastern reef  strikes north-south while the  Western reef  strikes west of north and dips to the east.
properties.work_desc: 2 shafts; 7.6 and 4m  deep,  3-4 adits longest 15m mostly filled in.

properties.summary_desc: The gold mineralisation was found in quartz leaders of unknown dimensions which were hosted by a ferruginous slate. The leader was mined by a 6m shaft (caved in) and trenching to shallow depths. Worked by Boehme and party in 1890's.
Davis and Party recovered gold from loam at Slaty Creek in Portion 189 Parish Ironbarks. No other information.
A 21m shaft dug for gold  in 1931 by Dixon and party at Nuggety Gully Hill in portion 248.. Deposit type and form unknown.
The workings are located on an auriferous quartz vein which strikes 290. Located in portion 28 and reportedly worked by McDermott and party in 1910's.
Stream sediment survey by BHBG in 1991 uncovered a weak Au anomaly 78.9 ppb. Source of the gold was probably quartz that outcrops in the vicinity. No follow up work done.
A 200 x 250m area of alluvial workings running NW-SE. No other information
properties.work_desc: alluvial workings over an area 200m x 250m.

properties.summary_desc: A 100 x 100m area of alluvial workings. No other information.
properties.work_desc: alluvial workings over 100 x 100 m area.

properties.summary_desc: A 300 x 300m area of alluvial workings. No other information.
An 300 x 200 m area of  workings that trends north-south. Reported to be workings in a quartz reef  by Thurlow (1995),  Kratos Uranium(1981) reports area as alluvial workings.
properties.work_desc: Shallow diggings over an area of 300x200m.

properties.summary_desc: A line of shallow pits about 30m wide and 100m long and trending north-south. The type of occurrence is unknown as they could have been dugfor alluvial or reef gold. Kratos Uranium sampled area in 1981 and got low assay values.
properties.work_desc: Line of shallow pits about 30m wide over strike length of 100m.

properties.summary_desc: A shaft and three small pits are present in a area of 50x20m. At this location the shales strike 350 and dip 70 W. Some quartz vein material is present on the dumps but no sulphides or alteration observed.
properties.work_desc: 1 shaft and 3 pits over an area of 50 x 20m trending 350.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: This Tertiary deep lead also includes the Digger Prince Mine. The wash is described as being 3-15m wide and averaging 0.2m thick with zones up to 0.7m thick and poorer values being found at  depth. A very patchy gold occurrence.

properties.summary_desc: This occurrence was not visited.and the location is approximate. The mineralisation is reported as being associated with quartz and consisting of antimony sulphides and oxides. Two small lodes are reported as croping out at surface about 30m apart.

properties.summary_desc: The Fords Creek Tertiary deep lead was 3-9m wide; and 5-23cm thick with the upper portion being below 4.5m of overbyrdon. The lead was covered by basalt from just below junction of  two Leads.  The Soverign Lead joins this lead.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: The Caledonian lead is 30 to 40 metres wide and 15 to 25 cm thick. The lead was covered by basalt for most of its extent. Tributaries of the Caledonian include the Grecian Bend, Victorian, Redgate, and Little Caledonian deep leads.

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: Discovered in 1870 by R Adams, this partly basalt filled Tertiary deep lead includes the Eureka Shaft. The lead contained wash dirt up to 91m wide and averaged 38cm thick. The deeper areas are under 18-30m of basalt.

properties.hostrocks: alluvium - Ungrouped Cenozoic sedimentary units;  basalt - Ungrouped Cenozoic igneous units - volcanic
properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)

properties.reference: Matson C.R. (1974c) ;  Matson C.R. (1975a)
properties.summary_desc: This is a Y shaped lead with the wash being 6-21m wide and an average of 25cm thick. The grades are recorded as being poorer at depth. This lead is distinguished by the number of nuggets that were recovered.

properties.summary_desc: Two lodes, 10 m apart striking 125, dip steeply NE. Both lodes are apparently strike equivalents. East lens proven to at least 28 m, 0.3-1 m wide, up to 7 m long. West lens comprises disseminated sulphides, proven to 10 m, 0.6-1 m wide (Brown et al 1992).

properties.hostrocks: basalt - Woolooma Formation;  jasper - Woolooma Formation
properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992)
properties.summary_desc: Infilled shaft and numerous shallow pits on metabasalt and jasper. Numerous thin quartz veins and some brecciation of jasper. At least 2 generations of veins, one subparallel to bedding, dipping steeply W, one trending 025, W dipping (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.all_names: Golden Gate Reef, Old Golden Gate
properties.hostrocks: basalt - Woolooma Formation;  jasper - Woolooma Formation
properties.reference: () MR01451;  Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: Cluster of collapsed shafts in metabasalt with vughy white quartz and some pyritic jasper. Blebs of pyrite in some metabasalt, gross trend of workings 5 deg. Quartz blocks up to 10cm thick, many rich in iron oxides (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.hostrocks: basalt - Woolooma Formation;  jasper - Woolooma Formation
properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: Shaft with timber collar in metabasalt & jasper. Some quartz and minor calcite veins. Disseminated boxworks and iron staining after pyrite (?) in metabasalt and jasper. Veins apparently unmineralized (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: Pits and trenches on hillside, in metabasalt. General strike 000. No outcrop in pits. Quartz on dumps is unmineralized, vughy, and shows voids after calcite (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: White quartz on dumps. Some metabasalt is pyritic. Strike 150, dip unknown. Extends 30 m along strike. Width of veins up to 3 cm (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992)
properties.summary_desc: Gold probably derived from redistributed Tertiary sediments (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.hostrocks: basalt - Woolooma Formation;  chert - Woolooma Formation
properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Carne J.E. (1908a)
properties.summary_desc: Workings have  collapsed. Some quartz-carbonate veins with minor iron oxide boxworks after pyrite. Some pyrite voids in metabasalt (after massive pyrite). Possible Cyprus type deposit, stratiform (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992)
properties.summary_desc: Scattered clusters of pits in Tertiary deep leads. Probably represent prospecting pits for gold or diamonds (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992)
properties.summary_desc: Alluvial diggings, largely comprising pits. One open shaft with windlass and ladderway, worked up to mid 1987. J. O'Neill ('Merryville') reports original mines recovered 1 dwt/dish from here (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: Adit 100 m down hill below workings, driven at 090. Workings up hill follow foliation in serpentinite. No quartz noted or any  mineralisation. Some joint faces have a thin, brown ferruginous coating.
properties.work_desc: Underground, open cut, shafts, adits, shallow pits

properties.summary_desc: Adits, open cuts & inclined shafts in serpentine. Chromite lumps up to 5 cm across on dumps, most with slickensided surfaces. Track to workings in gully on south side of spur (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.summary_desc: Irregular line of pits in serpentine and dolerite. No vein material obvious. Probable gold in joints or fault planes, or short, stockwork-like veins. Metahydrothermal with supergene enrichment (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: One group of shallow pits and an isolated single pit in dolerite. No obvious mineralization or veins. Workings parallel major structural and lithological strike, suggesting possible fault or joint control (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.hostrocks: dolerite - Woodsreef Melange;  harzburgite - Woodsreef Melange

properties.summary_desc: Pits and shallow shafts on harzburgite & serpentine, close to contact of serpentine & harzburgite. No obvious mineralisation, probably joint fills of gold. Workings very extensive, often as closely spaced, parallel lines (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992)
properties.summary_desc: Vein orientation locally 045, deposit strike approx 170 for 175 m. Metahydrothermal, multiple vein (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.summary_desc: Long, shallowly dipping quartz reef tested by numerous pits along ridge crest. Workings in gully on east expose vein surfaces, showing 25 E dip. Possible collapsed adit (Brown et al. 1992).

properties.reference: (1987) GS1987/042;  Brown R.E., Brownlow J.W. & Krynen J.P. (1992)

properties.summary_desc: The deep lead trends approximately 032 deg. There are 2 wash horizons separated by up to 4 m of white clay, exposed in the open-cut. Most of the gold has come from near the base of the lower wash unit which overlies bedrock (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The main workings are on the Eastern lode.There are two parallel lodes which strike at 118 deg - 155 deg t and dip vertically (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: Gossanous quartz is present on the dumps. The workings have been infilled.077 deg t, dip unknown (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: Prospecting shafts in the area have been filled in (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: A small pit has been sunk in a manganese showing on strike to the S, 70 m S of the portion boundary. The landowner reported that Mn oxides outcrop in the E boundary of portion 85, about 1 km to the E of the main workings (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987) ;  MacNevin A.A. & Holmes G.G. (1980)

properties.summary_desc: The vein quartz is vughy and crystalline. The reef is shown on Odernheimer's map, compiled in 1855 (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987) ;  Mines Inspector, Peel River Land & Mineral Co, Odernheimer, King P.G. (1885) MR04291
properties.summary_desc: The quartz vein is 1.0 m wide at surface; according to old records it is 0.15 m wide at a depth of 17 m. Has 058 deg t, dip 45 deg SE. The vein is split at the northeastern end; both splits have been stoped (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).
properties.work_desc: Underground workings, open cut, shafts and adits,

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: These are alluvial terrace deposits at the confluence of the Peel and Canns (formerly Jamiesons) Creek. Rich leads at the base were worked by shafts and, in the case of the Brumby Charlie, an adit reputed to be 50 m long (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).
properties.work_desc: Underground workings, dredging/slucing, shafts and adits

properties.summary_desc: The reef was not found. The reef possibly trends westerly or northwesterly.The area is littered with workings and dumps, mostly colluvial, which have obscured the Golden Hole line (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: () MR00718;   (1979) GS1979/001;  Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The old workings have collapsed and/or been filled in. The quartz on the dump is vughy and crystalline. This reef is one of the first worked at Bowling Alley Point, and it appears to have been rich near the surface (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Fitzpatrick K.R. (1975b) ;  Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The lode is a sparsely mineralized, subvertical-vertical quartz vein up to 0.30 m wide and strike 083 deg t. 086 deg t, dip near-vertical. The workings consist of a single shaft. Only minimal driving was carried out (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.all_names: Connollys Reef, Blairmore Mine, East and West Reef
properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987) ;  Peel River Land and Minerals Company (1885) GS1885/001
properties.summary_desc: Reef had 124 deg t, reputed dip 50-70 deg S.This is Odernheimer's (GS1885/001) East and West reef, which was intensively tested by the Peel Company under his supervision (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: A terrace of river gravel has been worked for gold. According to his map, Odernheimer's (GS1885/001) North and South Reef is present at the site.177 deg t, dip 60-70 deg W (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987) ;  Peel River Land and Minerals Company (1885) GS1885/001
properties.summary_desc: Reef has 040 deg t, dip not known (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: Reef has 172 deg t, dip 50 deg E. Gold was found in the reef in 1857 by D'uason and Party. A party of chinese worked the reef in the bed of the river and won $24000 worth of gold in 1873 (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: Banded cherts crop out about 30 m west of the workings. Reef to 0.30 m wide. 167 deg t , dip not known (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The workings have been put down on a sequence of carbonated basalts, andesites, and cherts. The dumps contain gossanous and vughy quartz. Horizontal (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.work_desc: Underground workings, open cut, shafts and adits,

properties.summary_desc: The quartz veins, which are probably discontinuous, pinch and swell to 0.5 m in width. Locally the quartz is vughy and crystalline. There is some small potential for alluvial scheelite in surrounding watercourses (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: An adit was apparently driven on a horizontal quartz vein system, 0.3 m wide. Vertical veins are present also. The workings are mostly filled and collapsed. No quartz was found on the dumps (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: Almost no quartz is present on the old dumps. According to the parish card, a rich pocket of gold was found in iron-stained sediment, 3 m below the surface in a flat reef (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: Cherty sediments are present on the dumps. Some vein quartz is also present. This prospect appears to lie east of the serpentinite belt; all other reefs lie to the west. Line of lode trends 170 deg t (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.all_names: Trevena Gold Mine, Trevenna Gold Mine

properties.summary_desc: The host rock is a highly altered, very lateritized serpentinite, locally sheared parallel to the line of the lode. A few quartz veinlets, some with pyrite, are present on the walls of the open cuts in the lode zone (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: Dump material: felsic? tuff, weathered, altered, containing quartz veins to 40mm; quartz is vughy. The reef is most probably a southern extension of the Folly line (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: Gilligan and Brownlow (1987)-the Quaternary alluvial deposits are 'worked out'. GR: 3207E 5160N to 3235E 5245N. Many tributaries were also extensively worked, total alluvial production in excess of 5t Au (McEvilly 2002).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987) ;  Peel River Land and Minerals Company (1885) GS1885/001

properties.all_names: Fogartys Antimony Mine, Nundle Antimony Mine
properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The stibnite occurs in short, vertical shoots to 3m in length. There is virtually no stibnite between shoots. Strike 170 deg t (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: A major fault is shown to pass through the mine, on the 1:250,000 sheet.The lenses are at least 20 mm wide (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.summary_desc: The vein was known to Odernheimer in 1855 (GS1885/001). There are several cuts, pits, and filled shafts in the vicinity, ?prospectors workings. The stibnite workings, too, have been filled in.The veins are 0.3-0.5 m wide (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987) ;  Titles, Mineral Resources NSW ()
properties.summary_desc: There are two groups of workings: 1. An overgrown, collapsed adit (or adits) striking about 050 deg T. 2. three unfilled ?shafts in a 30 m long line trending 040 deg T. Reef trending at 140 deg T, (right angles to the adit) (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The dumps are moderately extensive; the workings have all collapsed. The quartz is vughy in places, and cherty in others. Edwards and Wilson put in a 60 m drive for very little return. What Wright and Taylor did is not known (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).
properties.work_desc: Underground workings, open cut, shafts and adits,

properties.work_desc: Underground workings, shafts and shallow pits,

properties.summary_desc: The workings have collapsed at the various portals. One adit, right in the creek, may be accessible. The reef is 0.40-0.50m wide (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
properties.summary_desc: The reef worked here is possibly the northern extension of the Brown Snake Reef. A dump sample of pyritic volcanic rock assayed 0.1ppm gold,and 0.15ppm silver (Gilligan and Brownlow 1987).

properties.reference: Gilligan L.B. & Brownlow J.W. (1987) ;  Gilligan L.B., Brownlow J.W. & Cameron R.G. (1987)
